evidence: Campaign plan pledges to defend the Oregon Health Plan (Medicaid) from federal cuts; no expansion or rate pledge (2026).
Campaign plan says she will team up with other states to cut prescription drug costs; no specific board pledge (2026).
Signed SB 605 barring medical debt from consumer credit reports (Sept 2025).
Campaign plan would stop insurers using AI to deny claims, a related step short of ending prior authorization (2026).
Signed the POWER Act (2025) so data centers pay more of their own power costs; 2026 plan backs a pause on new data centers.
Campaign cites the FAIR Act (2025) shielding households from utility rate hikes and the POWER Act cost shift (2026).
Signed HB 3991 raising the gas tax (Nov 2025), then urged lawmakers to repeal it after a referendum qualified (Jan 2026).
Signed SB 1537 (Mar 2024), allowing one-time urban growth boundary expansions and creating a housing accountability office.
Executive orders set a 36,000-homes-a-year goal and declared a homelessness emergency (Jan 2023), since extended.
2026 campaign plan pledges to boost starter homes and down payment assistance for first-time buyers; no broker-fee stance.
Signed SB 611 (July 2023) tightening Oregon's cap on annual rent increases.
Oregon Kids Credit, a refundable child tax credit (HB 3235), became law on her desk (2023, ch. 538).
Campaign plan pledges a pathway to universal preschool statewide (2026).
Campaign plan would expand infant and toddler care; created a Child Care Infrastructure Fund (2026), short of universal care.
As House Speaker passed Oregon's paid family and medical leave program (2019), cited on her campaign site (2022).
Campaign site cites her backing of minimum wage increases (2016 law as Speaker); no new $15 pledge (2022).
2026 campaign plan pledges to protect abortion access; signed 2026 laws strengthening Oregon's shield law and Planned Parenthood funding.
Campaign plan pledges to stand up to ICE and block detention sites; signed data-privacy limits on enforcement, not a sensitive-site ban (2026).
Signed pharmacy benefit manager reform aimed at lowering drug costs (2024), a related step short of a price-setting board.
Budget address proposed GRID standards making data centers bring their own power or pay for new generation (Feb 2026).
Budget address urged PUC scrutiny of utility spending and an end to black-box rate settlements (Feb 2026).
Pressed PECO to withdraw a proposed rate increase (2026), short of a formal freeze or bill credits.
Budget address called for extending the PJM wholesale price cap for two more years (Feb 2026).
Housing Action Plan would modernize the Municipalities Planning Code to ease residential building and speed permits (Feb 2026).
Executive Order 2024-03 (Sept 2024) ordered a statewide Housing Action Plan; planning, not direct permit fast-tracking.
Raised the PHARE housing trust fund cap $10M a year to $100M by 2027 and proposed a $1B bond-backed infrastructure fund (2024-26).
Housing Action Plan lists expanding homeownership opportunities but no specific down payment program or broker-fee ban (Feb 2026).
Proposed capping rental application fees at screening costs and barring pre-viewing fees; funded eviction counsel (Feb 2026).
Signed the 2023 expansion of the Property Tax/Rent Rebate program for seniors and people with disabilities (2023).
Signed the Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit, a state earned income credit worth up to $805, and expanded the child care credit (2024).
Budget address said pre-K teachers are underpaid and the budget delivers for them; no universal pre-K pledge (Feb 2026).
Expanded the child and dependent care tax credit and proposed higher child care worker retention bonuses (2024-26), short of universal care.
Budget proposes expanding student-teacher stipends for recruitment, a narrower step than raising teacher salaries (Feb 2026).
Backed a Lifeline voucher program in 2023 budget talks, then line-item vetoed its $100M after Democratic opposition (Aug 2023).
Budget address praised the Inspector General's work and urged passing a state False Claims Act (Feb 2026).
Implemented automatic voter registration at PennDOT driver license centers administratively (Sept 2023).
Budget address again asked lawmakers to send him a bill raising the minimum wage to $15 (Feb 2026).
Said a Democratic trifecta would let Pennsylvania finally codify reproductive freedom in law (Oct 2026).
Vowed during the primary to improve Medicaid reimbursement for health care providers; no detailed figures (Sept 2026).
Rhode Home plan: a revolving loan fund to finance 20,000 homes over eight years, funded by a millionaire's tax (Mar 2026).
Rhode Home plan would set aside 5% of the fund for rent relief; no other renter protections specified (Mar 2026).
Proposed a new marginal income tax on earnings over $1 million, dedicated to the Rhode Home housing fund (Mar 2026).
Campaign plan pledges every Rhode Island family will have access to pre-K, i.e. universal pre-K (2026).
Campaign plan offers a $20M employer-matched child care pilot and expanded child care tax credits, short of universal care (2026).
Ballotpedia survey in her first governor run listed a middle-class tax cut as a priority (2022); no 2026 restatement found.
Ballotpedia survey in her first governor run pledged to protect the right to choose (2022); no 2026 codification stance found.
Campaign site would end special-interest property tax breaks for data centers and green energy; no pledge on power costs (May 2026).
Campaign site would eliminate property taxes on seniors' and veterans' homesteads, with a voter-approved senior exemption (May 2026).
Campaign site would make Oklahoma a no-income-tax state, a broader step than a targeted middle-class cut (May 2026).
Campaign site pledges to make Oklahoma teacher pay tops in the region, tied to performance (May 2026).
Campaign site proposes a state Department of Government Efficiency and performance-based budgeting; no inspector general pledge (May 2026).
Campaign platform would reduce and eliminate personal property taxes, including the car tax, for seniors and veterans (2026).
Campaign platform pledges to fight to eliminate the state income tax, broader than a targeted middle-class cut (2026).
Campaign platform would expand school choice, though it also pledges to fully fund public schools (2026).
Campaign platform backs state and local help for federal immigration enforcement, including 287(g) deals (2026).
Campaign platform pledges a comprehensive audit of state and local governments to root out fraud and waste (2026).
Campaign platform says he is pro-life and will always back laws to defend the unborn; defended SC abortion limits as AG (2026).
